value_stream.name: Workforce Background Screening, Credentialing & Personnel Vetting

fields.Participants: HR (VS-19), Hiring Manager, Screening vendor (W4867), Legal (VS-100.3), Adverse-Action Board (W4871)
fields.Trigger: Candidate selection (VS-121); offer-conditional on screening clearance

workflows.name: Employee Pre-Hire Screening Integration & Offer-Conditional Workflow

Automation Opportunity: - ATS → screening-order auto-trigger; consent e-signature; vendor-result ingestion; clear/flag workflow
Controls: - CTL-732 (ensure controlled execution — Vetting Operations Across Workforce Categories (PA-167.2).)
- CTL-732: consent before order; sensitive roles offer-conditional; chain-of-custody; recorded in HRIS
Cross-references: - links to VS-121 (recruiting), VS-19 (HR), VS-29 (worker record), W4866/W4868/W4869 (policy/consent/package), W4870 (evidence), W4877 (re-screening), W4880 (adverse-action)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Hire-before-clear risk**: Onboarding before screening clears (esp. sensitive roles) → negligent-hiring exposure; mitigated by offer-conditional for sensitive roles
- **Delay risk**: Slow screening losing candidates (esp. in a tight labor market); mitigated by SLA + parallel where lawful
- **Consent-gap risk**: Screening without consent → unlawful processing (W4868); mitigated by consent-before-order
System Touchpoints: - ATS/HRIS (VS-121/VS-19); screening platform/vendor (W4867); worker record (VS-29); records (VS-88); analytics (VS-28)

steps.activity: On candidate selection, trigger the screening order from the ATS/HRIS (VS-121): capture consent (W4868), determine the role-package (W4866/W4869), and order the package from the screening vendor; structure the offer as conditional-on-screening-clearance for sensitive roles
steps.r: Talent Acquisition / Screening Program Manager

steps.activity: Execute & verify: vendor runs the package (NBI/employment/etc.), Screening verifies authenticity and the chain-of-custody (W4870); track TAT against the SLA; for clear results, clear for hire; for adverse findings, route to the Adverse-Action Board (W4871/W4880)
steps.r: Screening Program Manager / Vendor

steps.activity: Record in the HRIS/worker record (VS-19/VS-29), file the evidence (W4872), set the re-screening schedule (W4877), and feed screening metrics to analytics (W4881); for adverse outcomes, manage the candidate per the fair-chance framework (W4880)
steps.r: Screening Program Manager / HR / Records

fields.Frequency: Per worker assignment (~10–20% of store/DC labor)
fields.Owner: Screening Program Manager / Contingent Workforce Coordinator (VS-98)
fields.Trigger: Contractor/outsourced-worker assignment (before site entry) (VS-98); agency onboarding
fields.Volume: ~600–1,200 contingent workers across 200 stores + 4 DCs (security, janitorial, promodizers, agency labor; ~10–20% of site labor per VS-98)

workflows.name: Contingent/Outsourced Worker Screening Governance & Agency Accountability

Automation Opportunity: - Agency-screening-record upload/audit; authenticity-verification (NBI portal); worker-clear badge
Controls: - CTL-732: agency contract specifies screening; BuildRight audits; high-risk roles enhanced; failures attributed
Cross-references: - links to VS-98 (contingent, W3223), VS-161 (TPRM), VS-159 (security), VS-23 (LP), W4869 (package), W4877 (re-screening), W4880 (adverse-action)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Agency-shirking risk**: Agencies certifying without actually screening; mitigated by BuildRight audits + authenticity verification
- **Insider-threat risk**: Unscreened contractor committing theft/fraud (W3229); mitigated by mandatory/enhanced screening
- **Accountability risk**: Screening failures unattributed; mitigated by agency-contract accountability
System Touchpoints: - Contingent workforce (VS-98); worker record (VS-29); agency/vendor master (VS-03); TPRM (VS-161); security (VS-159); records (VS-88)
Time Estimate: - ~per worker screening 1–5 days; agency governance continuous

steps.a: VP Legal & Compliance / Contingent Workforce Mgr
steps.activity: Govern the agency screening obligation (extends W3223): each agency certifies pre-engagement screening per BuildRight's role-package (cash-handling, security, child-adjacent critical), with BuildRight-specified checks (NBI, police, prior-employment, drug where lawful, court for cash/security); flow the obligation into the agency contract (VS-98)
steps.r: Screening Program Manager / Contingent Coordinator / Legal / Procurement

steps.activity: Verify agency screening quality: BuildRight audits agency screening records, verifies authenticity (NBI verification, sample re-check), and rejects uncertified workers; for high-risk roles (security, CIT VS-81, cash-handling, IT-admin) require enhanced screening + Security review (links to W3223/W4876)
steps.r: Screening Program Manager / Security / Contingent Coordinator

steps.activity: Manage re-screening (W4877), adverse-action (W4880), and records (W4872) for contingent workers; ensure agency accountability for screening failures and feed screening-compliance to TPRM (VS-161), VS-98 governance, and analytics (W4881)
steps.r: Screening Program Manager / Contingent Coordinator / TPRM

fields.Owner: Screening Program Manager / Procurement (VS-03/VS-34) / Store/DC Ops
fields.Trigger: Vendor/3PL personnel granted site access (delivery drivers VS-56/VS-110, service technicians, installers VS-12); partner onboarding
fields.Volume: ~600–1,200 vendor/3PL personnel across 200 stores + 4 DCs (per VS-98)

workflows.name: Vendor & 3PL Personnel Site-Access Vetting (Drivers, Delivery, Service)

Automation Opportunity: - Cleared-personnel roster; access-control auto-grant/revoke; driver-license auto-verification (W1400/W4754); partner-compliance dashboard
Controls: - CTL-732 (ensure controlled execution — Vetting Operations Across Workforce Categories (PA-167.2).)
- CTL-732: site-access vetting standard; partner contract flow-down; access only for cleared personnel; rosters current
Cross-references: - links to VS-56/VS-110 (3PL), VS-159 (security/access), VS-23 (LP), VS-161 (TPRM), W1400/W4754 (driver-license), W4881 (analytics)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Unvetted-access risk**: A vendor/3PL person accessing sites unvetted → theft/safety incident; mitigated by the standard + access-control integration
- **Stale-roster risk**: Personnel changed but access not revoked; mitigated by roster tracking
- **Partner-non-compliance risk**: Partner not certifying/verifying; mitigated by contract + audits
System Touchpoints: - Vendor master (VS-03/VS-29); 3PL (VS-56/VS-110); access control/security (VS-159); driver-license (W1400/W4754); TPRM (VS-161); LP (VS-23)
Time Estimate: - ~per personnel vetting hours–days; partner governance continuous

steps.a: VP Legal & Compliance / Chief Compliance & Security Officer
steps.activity: Define the site-access vetting standard for vendor/3PL personnel: identity verification, driver-license check (links to W1400/W4754 driver-license verification), NBI/basic screening for recurring-site-access roles (delivery, service, installation), and the access-control integration (badging, escorts)
steps.r: Screening Program Manager / Security / Procurement

steps.activity: Flow the standard into vendor/3PL contracts (VS-56/VS-110/VS-100.3): the partner certifies its personnel are vetted per the standard, BuildRight verifies (sample/license-authenticity), and access is granted only to cleared personnel; manage exceptions (one-time vs recurring access)
steps.r: Procurement / Legal / Screening Program Manager / Security

steps.activity: Monitor & enforce: track cleared-personnel rosters, revoke access on personnel change, audit partner compliance, and feed vendor-screening compliance to TPRM (VS-161) and analytics (W4881); manage any incident involving vendor personnel (links to VS-23/VS-159)
steps.r: Screening Program Manager / Security / TPRM / Store Ops

fields.Owner: Screening Program Manager / Corporate Security (VS-159) / Legal (VS-100.3)
fields.Participants: CHRO, Board/ nominating (VS-36), External counsel/vetting firm, DPO (VS-91)
fields.Trigger: Executive/sensitive-role hire/appointment (CEO/CFO/CIO/IT Security Manager, finance/treasury, security/CIT, IT-admin/data, buyer/procurement); periodic re-vet

Automation Opportunity: - Enhanced-vetting checklist; multi-source monitoring; sanctions/PEP/litigation screening (VS-86); confidentiality workflow
Controls: - CTL-732 (ensure controlled execution — Vetting Operations Across Workforce Categories (PA-167.2).)
- CTL-732: enhanced package per sensitive role; lawful basis + consent; confidential; findings to governance
Cross-references: - links to VS-159 (corporate security), VS-36 (board/nominating), VS-86 (sanctions/PEP), VS-119/W426 (COI), VS-91 (privacy), W4871 (adverse-action board), W4877 (re-vet)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Senior-negligent-appointment risk**: An unfit executive → fiduciary/reputational harm; mitigated by enhanced vetting
- **Confidentiality risk**: Executive screening data leaking → harm/liability; mitigated by strict confidentiality (VS-159/VS-91)
- **Privacy risk**: Over-intrusive enhanced vetting → RA 10173 exposure; mitigated by lawful basis + senior consent + proportionality
System Touchpoints: - Corporate security (VS-159); legal (VS-100.3); AML/sanctions (VS-86); ethics/COI (VS-119/W426); board governance (VS-36); privacy (VS-91)

steps.activity: Define the enhanced-vetting package for executives/sensitive roles: full NBI/court, multi-source media/reputational, sanctions/PEP/litigation (links to VS-86/VS-100), conflicts-of-interest (links to VS-119/W426), credit-for-finance, reference interviews, education/employment verification, and (for security/CIT) enhanced criminal; lawful under RA 10173 with senior consent
steps.r: Screening Program Manager / Corporate Security / Legal / DPO

steps.activity: Execute via specialized vetting firm/external counsel (where appropriate): conduct the enhanced package for board-appointed executives and sensitive roles, with strict confidentiality (VS-159), and route findings to the Adverse-Action Board (W4871) and nominating/governance committee (VS-36)
steps.r: Corporate Security / External Vetting Firm / Legal

steps.activity: Periodically re-vet (W4877) sensitive roles, manage adverse findings with due process (W4880), and ensure confidentiality/privacy of sensitive screening data (VS-91/W4872); feed executive-vetting outcomes to governance (VS-36)
steps.r: Screening Program Manager / Corporate Security / Legal

fields.Participants: Contingent Coordinator (VS-98), Legal (VS-100.3), LP (VS-23), Labor Relations (VS-84)
fields.Trigger: Re-screening cycle (annual/biennial per role); triggering event (arrest/conviction, sanctions listing, fraud/LP event, role change); continuous-monitoring alert

workflows.name: Periodic Re-Screening, Continuous Monitoring & Triggered Re-Vet

Automation Opportunity: - Continuous-monitoring feed (sanctions/criminal/media); event → re-vet trigger; re-screening scheduler
Controls: - CTL-732: periodic re-screening by role-tier; continuous monitoring on; triggers acted on with due process
Cross-references: - links to VS-86 (sanctions/PEP), VS-23/VS-125 (LP/fraud), VS-159 (insider-risk), VS-84 (labor), W4868 (consent), W4880 (adverse-action)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Stale-screening risk**: A worker screened years ago now flagged (arrest/sanctions) undetected; mitigated by re-screening + continuous monitoring
- **Trigger-miss risk**: A triggering event (LP complaint, arrest) not triggering re-vet; mitigated by event-linkage from VS-23/VS-84
- **Due-process risk**: Acting on a triggering event without due process → NLRC exposure; mitigated by the individualized assessment (W4880)
System Touchpoints: - Screening platform; workforce roster (VS-29); sanctions/AML (VS-86); LP/fraud (VS-23/VS-125); security/insider-risk (VS-159); labor (VS-84)

steps.activity: Maintain the re-screening schedule (role-tier-based periodicity) and the continuous-monitoring feed (sanctions/PEP watchlist links to VS-86, criminal/court monitoring where lawful, media/reputational for sensitive roles); reconcile to the workforce roster (VS-29)
steps.r: Screening Program Manager / Security / HR

steps.activity: Manage triggered re-vet: on a triggering event (an arrest/conviction, a sanctions listing, an LP/fraud event VS-23/VS-125, a role change to higher-risk, a complaint), re-screen the individual with consent (W4868) and route findings to the Adverse-Action Board (W4871/W4880)
steps.r: Screening Program Manager / Security / Legal

steps.activity: Decide & act: clear (no action), enhanced-monitor, restrict duties, or separate (W4880) per the individualized assessment and due process; document in the chain-of-custody (W4870) and feed re-screening outcomes to insider-risk (VS-23/VS-159) and analytics (W4881)
steps.r: Screening Program Manager / HR / Security / Labor Relations

fields.Owner: Screening Program Manager / HR Shared Services (VS-103)
fields.Participants: Entity HR, Legal (VS-100.3), DPO (VS-91), Labor Relations (VS-84)
fields.Trigger: Cross-entity hire/transfer; regional onboarding; consistency audit

workflows.name: Cross-Entity (5 Entities) & Regional Screening Consistency & Transfer Handling

Automation Opportunity: - Cross-entity screening-standard enforcement; transfer re-screen trigger; consistency/bias dashboard
Controls: - CTL-732 (ensure controlled execution — Vetting Operations Across Workforce Categories (PA-167.2).)
- CTL-732: unified policy across entities; transfers screened-to-standard; consistency audited
Cross-references: - links to VS-103 (HR shared services), VS-29 (roster), VS-91 (privacy), VS-84 (labor), W4866/W4869 (policy/package), W4870 (chain-of-custody), W4871 (bias)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Inconsistency risk**: Different entities screening differently → fairness/legal risk; mitigated by the unified policy
- **Transfer-gap risk**: A transfer with a screening gap (new role needs deeper screen); mitigated by transfer re-screen
- **Regional-variation risk**: Lawful regional differences mishandled; mitigated by documented variations + Legal review
System Touchpoints: - HR shared services/HRIS (VS-103/VS-19); workforce roster (VS-29); legal (VS-100.3); privacy (VS-91); audit (VS-21)

steps.activity: Maintain cross-entity consistency: the screening policy (W4866) and packages (W4869) apply uniformly across the 5 entities (Depot, Logistics, Digital Commerce, Property Mgmt, Holdings) and regions, with documented regional variations only where lawful/source-different (e.g., regional court-records availability)
steps.r: Screening Program Manager / HR Shared Services / Legal

steps.activity: Handle transfers: when an employee transfers across entities or regions, verify prior screening meets the new role/entity standard, re-screen gaps, port the screening record (chain-of-custody W4870) with consent (W4868), and update the workforce roster (VS-29)
steps.r: HR Shared Services / Screening Program Manager

steps.activity: Audit consistency: periodically audit entity/region screening for policy adherence and bias indicators (W4871); remediate inconsistencies; report consistency to governance (W4888) and analytics (W4881)
steps.r: Screening Program Manager / Internal Audit (VS-21) / HR Shared Services

fields.Owner: Screening Program Manager / Occupational Health (VS-83) / Drug-Free Program (VS-150)
fields.Trigger: Screening package includes drug/health/license checks (W4869); safety-sensitive role
fields.Volume: ~2,000–3,000 safety-sensitive staff (drivers, forklift, paint/chemical handlers, security)

Automation Opportunity: - Integrated-package orchestration; clinic/drug/license result ingestion; safety-sensitive clearance gate
Controls: - CTL-732: drug/health/license checks per safety-sensitive role; lawful testing; clearance gate; due process
Cross-references: - links to VS-83 (clinic/health), VS-150 (drug-free), VS-06/W1400 (driver license), W600/W558 (PRC/TESDA), W4869 (package), W4870 (chain-of-custody), W4880 (adverse-action)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Safety risk**: A drug/health/license issue undetected in a safety-sensitive role → incident; mitigated by integrated screening + clearance gate
- **Lawful-testing risk**: Non-compliant drug testing (VS-150 DOLE D.O. 53-03); mitigated by the drug-free program
- **Due-process risk**: Acting on a finding without due process; mitigated by W4880
System Touchpoints: - Occupational health/clinic (VS-83); drug-free (VS-150); fleet/driver (VS-06/W1400); PRC/TESDA (W600/W558); screening platform; legal (VS-100.3)
Time Estimate: - ~per screen days; continuous for periodic checks

steps.activity: Integrate drug-test (VS-150), occupational-health (VS-83), and license checks (driver W1400/W4754, PRC/TESDA W600/W558) into the screening package for relevant roles (drivers, forklift/reach operators, paint/chemical handlers, security, PRC-licensed engineers); define the integrated package per role
steps.r: Screening Program Manager / Occupational Health / Drug-Free Officer

steps.activity: Execute via the clinic (VS-83) and the drug-free program (VS-150) with consent (W4868), lawful testing (DOLE D.O. 53-03 per VS-150), and license verification; manage results through the chain-of-custody (W4870)
steps.r: Occupational Health / Drug-Free Officer / Screening Program Manager

steps.activity: Manage adverse health/drug/license findings via the Adverse-Action Board (W4871/W4880) with due process (VS-150 substance-abuse due process, VS-84 NLRC); ensure safety-sensitive roles are not placed without clearance; feed integrated-screening metrics to analytics (W4881)
steps.r: Screening Program Manager / Drug-Free Officer / Legal

fields.Owner: Adverse-Action Review Board (W4871) / Legal (VS-100.3) / Labor Relations (VS-84)
fields.Participants: HR, Screening Program Manager, Security (VS-159), DPO (VS-91)
fields.Trigger: Adverse screening finding (employee/contingent/vendor/executive); dispute/appeal; NLRC complaint

Automation Opportunity: - Individualized-assessment decision tool; pre-adverse-action notice automation; bias-indicator dashboard; appeal tracker
Controls: - CTL-732 (ensure controlled execution — Vetting Operations Across Workforce Categories (PA-167.2).)
- CTL-732: individualized assessment; pre-adverse-action notice; due process; bias monitored
Cross-references: - links to VS-84 (labor/NLRC), VS-91 (privacy), VS-159 (security), VS-100.3 (legal), VS-19 (separation), W4866 (fair-chance), W4871 (review board), W4883 (false-document), W4888 (governance)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Wrongful-decision risk**: A wrongful disqualification → NLRC/human-rights claim + lost talent; mitigated by individualized assessment + due process
- **Bias/disparate-impact risk**: Adverse actions disparately affecting a protected group; mitigated by bias-indicator monitoring
- **Inconsistent-decision risk**: Similar findings decided differently; mitigated by the Review Board + framework
System Touchpoints: - Screening/HRIS platform; legal (VS-100.3); labor relations (VS-84); privacy (VS-91); records (VS-88); analytics (VS-28)

steps.activity: On an adverse finding, conduct the individualized assessment (W4866 — nature/gravity/time-since/relevance-to-role/rehabilitation), issue the pre-adverse-action notice, allow the individual to respond/dispute/evidence rehabilitation, and verify the finding's accuracy (W4883 false-document risk)
steps.r: Review Board / Legal / Screening Program Manager

steps.activity: Decide: clear (no action), conditional (enhanced monitoring/restrictions), or disqualify (withdraw offer / restrict duties / separate); document the decision and notice with due-process alignment (VS-84 NLRC); for separations, coordinate with VS-19 separation and VS-84 labor relations
steps.r: Review Board / HR / Labor Relations / Legal

steps.activity: Manage appeals & NLRC complaints (VS-84): the appeal path, evidence preservation (W4872), and labor-case defense; track adverse-action outcomes and bias indicators (W4871) to governance (W4888) and analytics (W4881)
steps.r: Legal / Labor Relations / Review Board
